about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.
plan: Shared by all six shots and recorded in README.md's capture block: window 1440x763 on the deployed build at ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.boot(); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30), then DEV.cam(...) and one DEV.tick(1) per shot, vitals pinned at 100, the level's own hostiles cleared (never DEV.clear()), level banner taken down with banner('', 0). A frozen clock does not stop S.t, so these frames are reproducible by statistics and never by md5. **One term this plan did not record: the audio device.** A live boot advances the seeded stream through SND.init's noise buffer before the generator runs, so one seed deals one level per sample rate (#404, and the rule the tool prints as HW_WHY). These six captures read no SND.ac.sampleRate, so every row carries `sampleRate: null`, `check` prints each one as a device-scoped deal, and the binding below is per-machine: it says this frame is what ?dev=1&seed=60 dealt on the capture's audio device, not that every machine deals it. `STRICT=1 node tools/recap.js check` gates the missing term. A capture that reads the rate turns its own row into a cross-machine binding with no change to the tool.

The reference shot for the block: the route and every deal field in these six rows are transcribed from README.md's capture block (deployed build, ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.layoutSig 735688443, js blobs md5-identical to ce9d39d) rather than re-measured here. #335 measured this route: reloading the same URL read DEV.seed 60 and layout 735688443 on both loads, which is what makes origin+install=url-open a binding route.

Re-taken at 8eade8f (#388, fourth frame for this seat) because main took #400 take two - a wall fixture is now a box standing off the face, with a dimmed flank - while the previous capture of this row was in review, and the caption credits #400 for a shape the shipped pixels have to actually show. The build field now names c6a9b4c, the build the deployed page serves and the one this branch merges; these pixels were drawn at 8eade8f and the only blob that differs between the two, js/13_mesh.js (a9f01984 -> c2f98a53, #376), moves no pixel at this seat - SEAT=1.5,2.5,0.6 node tools/view.js scene 3 renders the SAME framebuffer md5 (d65879e5) against both js/ trees, because #376 substitutes identity for a room hue that reads MAP.lt 128/128/128 here anyway. No re-render was needed and none was done: sha256 is the same one the previous row carried. Route is the same instrument as the other five and is the URL itself: headless Chromium opened this row's url with a 1440x763 device-metrics override at scale 1, and the route ran from a Runtime.evaluate once the page reported ready: DEV.boot(); startLevel(3, true); banner(', 0); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30); P.hp = 100; DEV.cam(1.5, 2.5, floorAt(1.5, 2.5), 0.60, 0); DEV.tick(1); the level's own 4 hostiles left standing. Two route facts. (a) A page that never acquires a pointer lock pauses on the first blur and the pause overlay dims everything beneath it, so the route re-checks S.mode !== 'play' and calls the game's own resume() plus one more DEV.tick(1), immediately before the screenshot as well as after the route; this capture read 'play' at all four probes. Forgetting that step gives a paused frame reading 14.52 mean - caught by decoding the PNG, not by trusting the canvas. It is also why the route is NOT injected at document time any more: injected early it finishes before the first blur, the page pauses again afterwards, and the capture is a dimmed frame that reports S.mode play at the moment the route returns. (b) The deployed index.html and all eleven js/ blobs were read over the wire again at this head (2026-10-08, through the egress proxy) and are md5-identical to this merged tree's js/ - js/40_render.js 5f4726b7, js/20_level.js 5792aeb3 and js/13_mesh.js c2f98a53 included, index.html 44b7f0ca - so route, served page and tree name one build again, which is the claim this row exists to make. FIX_DEP reads {DOOR 0.12, PIPE 0.10, STRIPE 0.03, VENT 0.08} in the live page and DECOR reads 14, so the caption's stood-off fixture is a term of the build that drew this frame. layout 2733654509 is DEV.layoutSig() read back after that route, so it names the deal THESE pixels show - and the re-read this head asked for says that number is a property of the capture RUN and not of the URL: two runs of the documented route on the deployed page, the route issued the moment the page reported ready (2.23 s and 2.27 s after launch, S.mode read play at all four probes), both read 3233039185; a run whose route ran several seconds after ready read 1900969947; and inside one already-open page, DEV.tick(300) then startLevel(3, true) read 1730990788 and a second startLevel with no ticks read 1523817166. startLevel generates from wherever the seeded stream has reached and generation advances it, so one seed re-deals on every run. A capture taken that way decodes 50.39 (thirds 41.85 / 58.49 / 50.87) and differs from these bytes by 23,383 px over 2 luma - a different panel deal at the same room and the same geometry, rows 300-330 reading 38.2 in both - which is the deal moving, not the build: the two js/ trees are framebuffer-identical at this seat as named above. MAP.fz is authored and unchanged; the MAP.cell half is what moves, because #400's fixture placement draws from the seeded stream the wall panels are picked from. Geometry and tone reproduce, panel choice does not, and re-running this route is not a way to re-take this frame - pinning the stream before startLevel, the way tools/view.js does at a deal, would be. SND.ac.sampleRate read 44100, so this row is a cross-machine binding where the other five are device-scoped. Frame mean luma 50.54, thirds 41.8 / 58.9 / 50.9, channels 49.6 / 51.1 / 47.7; against the bytes it replaces, 15,807 px move by more than 2 luma, 13,184 of them in the middle third, filling one band x 660-1295 x y 340-422 (the TECH wall face and the far ceiling strip above it, 71.4 there -> 87.5 here, worst 90 luma). No renderer term is in that delta: rows 300-330 read 38.2 in both frames and the 4.00 plane at rows 140-180 reads 44.7 in both. The band is the deal's panel choice, not a lighting change.
